turns.title: Contact in the strait
turns.inject: A Meridian coast-guard cutter shadows a Blue-flag survey vessel inside contested waters. Red naval assets reposition to the north shoal while civilian traffic continues through the shipping lane. Both capitals receive the report within the hour.

memo.situation: Survey vessel shadowed; no shots fired; shipping lane open.
memo.decision: Open a deconfliction channel and hold the survey vessel on station
memo.rationale: Withdrawal concedes the legal position; an escort risks a bump incident inside a crowded lane. A standing deconfliction channel preserves the claim while lowering the chance of miscalculation, and it costs nothing to keep the frigate over the horizon as a hedge.

memo.situation: Blue survey activity inside claimed waters; cutter in visual range.
memo.decision: Continue shadowing and file a formal protest
memo.rationale: Boarding forces Blue to respond and hands them the escalation narrative. Shadowing documents presence, sustains the claim, and keeps every option open for the next move.

memo.situation: Two capitals postured but talking through public channels only.
memo.decision: Offer neutral-flag observers for the strait
memo.rationale: Observers give both sides a face-saving reason to keep distance and create an evidentiary record that discourages staged incidents.

adjudication.narrative: The cutter holds a half-mile off the survey vessel through the night. Blue's deconfliction request is acknowledged but unanswered. Red's protest lands at the regional forum as the mediator's observer offer circulates. No contact; the lane stays open.

turns.title: The shoal incident
turns.inject: At dawn a Red corvette crosses the survey vessel's bow at four hundred meters, forcing an emergency turn. Deck footage reaches social media within minutes. Blue's frigate is ninety minutes out. Domestic pressure spikes in both capitals.

memo.situation: Near-collision on record; public pressure to respond; frigate inbound.
options: Close the frigate to escort range
memo.decision: Close the frigate to escort range and publish the deconfliction transcript
memo.rationale: The transcript shows Blue asked for deconfliction before the incident, which frames the escort as protective rather than escalatory. Escort range restores deterrence without entering weapons release posture. Withdrawing under coercion now would invite a repeat at every future survey.

memo.situation: Corvette maneuver exceeded shadowing guidance; video is public.
memo.decision: Recall the corvette and quietly accept observers
memo.rationale: The maneuver overstepped the shadowing order. Recall under a maintenance cover avoids rewarding the local commander while the observer framework caps Blue's escort presence, which is now inevitable.

memo.situation: Viral incident; both sides seeking off-ramps that do not look like retreat.
memo.rationale: Pairing the standstill with observers gives both navies a scheduled, inspectable reason to hold position while the news cycle cools.

verdict.note: unsafe maneuver plus armed escort in proximity
recall-under-cover is a documented de-escalation pattern

adjudication.narrative: The frigate takes escort station at one nautical mile as the corvette turns for port. Red's foreign ministry calls the recall 'routine maintenance'; nobody believes it and nobody challenges it. Observer boarding is scheduled inside the standstill window. The strait is quieter at dusk than at dawn.

debriefs.text: The deconfliction channel opened in turn 0 was the load-bearing move: it converted the turn 1 escort from an escalation into a documented protective response. Publishing the transcript spent a one-time asset; future runs should weigh holding it for adjudication instead.

The corvette maneuver was a subordinate overstep the shadowing order made possible. Tighter rules of engagement in the turn 0 order would have prevented the viral incident and preserved the protest-track advantage.
Both parties wanted off-ramps by turn 1; the mediator's job was sequencing. Offering observers before the incident made accepting them after it look like process rather than concession.
